newsitem.title: CROATIA: Serb enclave's railway rejoins Croatia network.
newsitem.headline: Serb enclave's railway rejoins Croatia network.

text.p: Serb railways in Eastern Slavonia were integrated into the rail network of their former Croatian foes on Friday, weeks before Zagreb is due to assume authority over the last Serb enclave.

The accord on re-integration of all railway facilities and employees of the region into the Republic of Croatia was signed in Vukovar by Croat and Serb officials and witnessed by the United Nations Transitional Authority.
Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb enclave in Croatia, is administered by the United Nations, whose current mandate ends on July 15 when the area is due to come under Croatian government control.
"We consider this as a very important additional step in the peaceful reintegration of the region," Soren Serederian, deputy to UNTAES chief General Jacques Klein, told reporters.

"This re-integration will enable a link between Croatia and Yugoslavia shortly. This act ... creates preconditions for economic and all other contacts," said Stevo Novakovic, the area's Serb secretary for transport and communications.
The Croatian side hailed the accord as extremely important and said it was just a stepping stone for further opening up to the world.

"We want to go on, to open border crossings as soon as possible so that transit transport can start going towards Hungary, Yugoslavia and Bosnia," said Djurica Misin, deputy manager of Croatian railways.
Eastern Slavonia, together with two other enclaves, was seized by its Serb minority in 1991 when they revolted against Croatia's secession from federal Yugoslavia.
Croatia recaptured all other Serb-held territory in a lightning offensive in 1995.
Eastern Slavonia is a fertile, oil-rich plain along the Danube bordering Yugoslavia and Hungary and it sustained immense damage in the bitter six-month war in 1991.
The international community has pledged millions of dollars in aid once the region peacefully rejoins Croatia.
"So far minimum funds had been invested in rebuilding of the railways. The damage (to the railroad) in the region is estimated at 150 million German marks," Novakovic said.
Croatian railways have pledged to retain all 312 Serb employees in the area, the U.N. said.
"We have now two lines operating Vinkovci-Tovarnik and Vinkovci-Vukovar. We hope in a very brief period of time to have the Osijek-Beli Manastir-Hungary line operating," Serederian said.
